about.title: About and how buying works — Hanna Vavilava
about.description: I have sold horses since 2016, and only show jumpers since 2021. Five steps: enquiry, phone call, viewing, pre-purchase exam, contract.
about.label: About
about.portraitAlt: Hanna Vavilava on a bay horse in an orange winner's rug, wearing a championship sash, in a show arena
about.bio: I have sold horses since 2016, and since 2021 only show jumpers that I choose and train myself. Between three and six horses stand in the stable at any one time — I ride each of them myself for at least four months before it appears on this site. I speak Polish and English, and I answer myself, with no intermediary.

faq.title: Questions — Hanna Vavilava
faq.description: Price negotiation, the pre-purchase exam, buying without travelling to Poland, trial periods and viewing lead times — the six questions I am asked most.
faq.label: Questions · 06
faq.heading: The questions I am asked most.
faq.intro: If something is missing here, just ask — I answer myself.

items.a: Prices are stated exactly and are the prices the horses sell for. I do not raise the asking price only to lower it later. If the pre-purchase exam finds something I did not list on the horse's page, we talk about the price or about calling the sale off.

items.q: Who carries out the pre-purchase exam?
items.a: A vet chosen by the buyer. I do not insist on a clinic or a vet. The buyer pays for the exam, and the horse is available at the stable on the agreed day.

items.q: Can I buy a horse without travelling to Poland?
items.a: Yes, but not on the strength of a video alone. The order is always the same: a phone call, the full uncut footage, a pre-purchase exam by a vet of your choice, and a viewing by someone you trust. The buyer makes the decision, not me.

items.q: What happens once I decide to buy?
items.a: A written contract describing the horse, the price and its health on the day of sale, then payment and a date for collection. We arrange the collection directly, not through the site.
No. Instead I offer as many rides as you like during the visit, full uncut recordings and a pre-purchase exam as thorough as you choose.

items.q: How long does it take to arrange a viewing?
items.a: Three to five working days. Viewings are at {stables}. The horses are in training — I need a day to prepare the horse and book a rider to present it.

faq.band: A question with no answer here? I reply within the hour, {hours}.

privacy.title: Privacy — Hanna Vavilava
privacy.description: How personal data is processed on this site.
privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.heading: How personal data is processed
privacy.intro: The notice under Article 13 GDPR for anyone who visits this site, sends an enquiry through its forms or signs up for new-horse emails.

controller.lead: The controller of personal data is:
controller.contact: For anything about personal data, write to {email}.

data.h: What data, why, and on what basis
p: An enquiry about a horse: name, country, WhatsApp number, optionally an Instagram account and a message, riding level, budget and buying timeframe. An enquiry for a horse not on the list: a WhatsApp number and the wishes described. Both carry the language and address of the page the form was sent from, and where the visitor came from (UTM tags, for example). This data is used to answer the enquiry and present an offer — steps taken at the request of the person concerned before entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

New-horse emails: the email address, the language, and when the signup was made and confirmed. We send that address one message with a confirmation link and, once confirmed, one message whenever a new horse comes up for sale. The basis is consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which is also the consent to direct marketing by electronic means. It can be withdrawn at any time with the link in every email, without affecting the lawfulness of what was sent before.

Protecting the forms: the IP address and browser data help tell a person from a bot and limit the number of enquiries from one address. The IP address is not stored. The basis is the controller's legitimate interest in keeping spam off the contact channel (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Running the site: on every visit the server processes the IP address and request data to deliver the page and protect it from abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

Visit statistics: page views and a few events are counted, sending an enquiry for example. The statistics use no cookies and store nothing on the device. A visit is recognised by a hash of the IP address and browser with a salt that changes daily, so it cannot be linked to a person or to a visit on another day. The page address is sent without the part after the # sign. The basis is legitimate interest: knowing which parts of the site work (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

processors.h: Who processes data on our behalf
processors.intro: The following service providers process data on the controller's behalf:

items.name: Google (Firebase)
items.role: hosting the site, the function that handles the forms (Warsaw) and the database holding the enquiries and the new-horse list (Belgium).

items.name: Microsoft (Microsoft 365)
items.role: the mailbox that receives a copy of every enquiry.

items.name: Resend
items.role: sends that copy by email, and the signup confirmations and new-horse emails, from servers in the European Union.

items.name: Telegram
items.role: the messenger in which Hanna Vavilava is notified of a new enquiry, with its content.

items.name: Umami Software, Inc. (Umami Cloud)
items.role: the visit statistics described above, on an account in the EU region.

items.name: Cloudflare (R2)
items.role: stores and serves the videos and the X-ray reports from our own subdomain, {media}. It sets no cookie, so it needs no consent — these are plain files, not a player embedded from someone else's service.

p: Some of these providers are based in the United States. Where data leaves the European Economic Area, the basis is the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission. Telegram operates outside the EEA, and notifications there are governed by its own privacy policy.

The published radiograph reports name the vet who carried out the examination and no other person: the horse's owner is removed before publication. A horse is not a person, so the rest of a report is not personal data.
An enquiry is deleted from the database, the mailbox and Telegram six months after it has been handled. If it ends in the sale of a horse, it is kept for as long as tax and accounting law requires.
An address on the new-horse list is kept until it unsubscribes, and unsubscribing deletes it at once. A signup not confirmed within 7 days expires and is deleted.
An enquiry that fails the Turnstile check is never stored anywhere. The visit statistics hold no personal data, because a hash with a daily-changing salt cannot be reversed.

You have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict its processing and to receive it in a portable form, and to object to processing based on legitimate interest (Articles 15–21 GDPR). To exercise them, write to {email}. You will have an answer within a month.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes UODO, ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw).
Providing data is voluntary, but without the fields marked as required an enquiry cannot be answered. The new-horse signup is separate from any enquiry and no answer depends on it.
The data is not used for automated decision-making or profiling. The Turnstile check only filters out bots and has no legal effect on anyone.
The WhatsApp and Telegram links open a chat in those apps. What you write there they process on their own terms, as separate controllers.

This site sets no cookies and stores nothing on your device, which is why it asks for no consent. Your browser keeps its own cached copies of pages and photos to load them faster; you can clear them at any time.

The videos are plain files from our own subdomain, {media}, not a player embedded from someone else's service. A film on a horse's page is downloaded only once you press play; before that, only its still frame. The short loop on the homepage downloads straight away, unless the browser asks for reduced motion or data saving, or the connection is slow. Either way, your browser downloads the film from Cloudflare R2, which sees the IP address like any server and sets no cookie. The play is counted in the statistics as an event, also without cookies.

When you start filling in an enquiry or new-horse signup form, the page loads Cloudflare Turnstile. Cloudflare may then store its own security cookies on the device. They are strictly necessary to tell a person from a bot, so they need no consent.

privacy.turnstile: The enquiry and new-horse signup forms are protected from spam by Cloudflare Turnstile. When someone starts filling in a form, Cloudflare processes their IP address and browser data to tell a person from a bot. The basis is legitimate interest: keeping spam off the channel buyers use to reach Hanna (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). An enquiry that fails the check is never stored.
